ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Pulse deficit

A patient undergoing monitoring has sinus beats alternating with PVCs. The monitor displays 90 ventricular complexes per minute, but the radial pulse is only 45/min. Blood pressure remains stable. Which mechanism best explains the difference between the electrical and palpable rates?

  1. The sinus node is firing at 180/min
  2. Every PVC is conducted backward through the AV node
  3. Complete heart block prevents all ventricular ejection
  4. Some premature beats eject insufficient blood to create a palpable pulse
  5. Half of the ECG complexes are necessarily equipment artifact
Answer and explanation

Some premature beats eject insufficient blood to create a palpable pulse

Short filling time can make ectopic beats mechanically weak, creating a pulse deficit.

Option explanations

Some premature beats eject insufficient blood to create a palpable pulse: Short filling time can make ectopic beats mechanically weak, creating a pulse deficit.

Half of the ECG complexes are necessarily equipment artifact: The consistent ECG morphology supports real ectopy; artifact is not required.

The sinus node is firing at 180/min: No finding supports a sinus rate of 180/min.

Every PVC is conducted backward through the AV node: Retrograde conduction is not the explanation for weak forward stroke volume.

Complete heart block prevents all ventricular ejection: Complete block does not prevent all ventricular contraction.
